speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. To better understand the nature of your shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I will ask you a few specific questions to guide our evaluation. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus Dislocation (Secondary Ossicular Chain Disruption)

The specific complaint of shooting pain when chewing, combined with the history of recurrent ear infections and your age, strongly suggests a mechanical issue with your ear bones rather than simple scar tissue. This often occurs when the ossicles become detached or dislocated after the initial healing phase. Have you noticed any change in the sensation of fullness or hearing fluctuation in that ear recently?
